bull.b: The Phase 2b findings provide objective evidence that PrimeC may slow disease progression in ALS, supported by an independent biomarker platform and previously reported functional and biological outcomes. This strengthens the clinical rationale for advancing the lead program over the next several quarters.

An expanded evidence package containing biomarker and clinical data can improve the quality of the regulatory review and strengthen PrimeC’s commercialization pathway. Health Canada’s lack of concern about the revised timetable indicates continued regulatory engagement despite the later March 2027 filing target.

Expanding PrimeC’s intellectual-property scope beyond ALS could create additional development and partnership opportunities if the application progresses. Targeting traumatic brain injury also broadens the potential addressable disease portfolio while preserving ALS as the company’s core priority.

bear.b: The absence of product revenue means NeuroSense has not yet demonstrated commercial monetization, while sizable recurring losses continue to fund development. Without a successful regulatory or commercialization milestone, the company’s earnings profile remains dependent on future execution rather than an established operating business.

Sustained and materially larger cash outflows increase the amount of capital required to maintain clinical programs and corporate operations. Even with some improvement in 2025, ongoing negative operating and free cash flow indicates that internal cash generation is not yet sufficient to support the business.

Negative equity and a sharply reduced asset base indicate that cumulative losses have weakened financial flexibility. Although absolute debt is low, this deterioration can constrain the company’s ability to absorb setbacks, fund development internally, or negotiate from strength when seeking additional capital.
